_title: Trains from France to Italy: 2026 Guide — WoW Train · glosx.app
_desc: Train routes from France to Italy in 2026 — Paris to Milan, Lyon to Turin, Nice to Genoa. Direct services, travel times and booking tips.
b1: By WoW Train · Updated July 2026 · 4 min read
b2: Crossing from France into Italy by train means passing through the Alps — one of the great journeys in European rail. The fastest connection is Lyon to Turin in 3 hours 30 minutes; from Paris, direct TGV trains reach Milan in around 7 hours.
b3: All routes from France to Italy by train
b4: Which train crosses from France to Italy?
b5: The main France-Italy rail corridor crosses the Alps via two routes: the Mont Cenis tunnel on the Lyon–Turin line, and the coastal route from Nice along the Ligurian coast to Genoa. TGV high-speed trains serve the Lyon–Turin corridor; regional and Intercity trains serve the coastal route.
b6: For Paris to Milan, the TGV crosses into Italy via the Fréjus tunnel, running through Modane and the Italian Alps before descending into the Po plain.
b7: How long is the train from France to Italy?
b11: Paris to Rome: ~10–11h with one change at Milan
b12: Paris to Florence: ~9h with one change at Milan
b13: Tips for booking France to Italy trains
b14: Book the TGV leg early. Paris–Milan TGV fares are dynamic and cheapest several weeks in advance.
b15: Connect in Milan or Turin. Both are major hubs with fast onward Frecciarossa services to Rome, Florence and Venice.
b16: Consider the scenic coastal route from Nice to Genoa if you have time — it hugs the Ligurian coast through Monaco and into Italy.

b20: Is there a direct train from France to Italy?
b21: Yes. Direct TGV trains connect Paris to Milan in ~7 hours and Lyon to Turin in ~3h 30m, crossing the Alps via tunnel.
b22: How long does the train from France to Italy take?
b23: The fastest connection is Lyon to Turin in approximately 3 hours 30 minutes. Paris to Milan takes around 7 hours on the direct TGV.
b24: Which is the best train route from France to Italy?
b25: For speed, Lyon to Turin is the best option. For Paris travellers heading to Rome or Florence, take the direct TGV to Milan and connect to a Frecciarossa — under 10 hours total.
